futureProcess: Write one lead/support/static beat table before implementation, including the cause of attention, the semantic ending and the final hold. For this scene the question and interface remain static while antenna, gaze, head and hand perform their distinct roles.
Keep interface feedback timings separate from the character timeline. Review immediate input responsiveness independently of the deliberately requested investigation duration.
Run controlled, reversible alternatives at matched size, theme and common opening. Change one gesture or repetition decision per audition and retain the control until the result earns adoption.
Use continuous playback to decide whether a thought or joke lands; use decoded frames and source timings to diagnose the particular moment. Explicitly record when continuous evidence is absent.

Include replay, cancellation and incoming-emotion continuity in the storyboard review, then provide the same constraints to engineering. Mechanical interruption success and a coherent incoming intention are separate checks.
Include first-view and scrolled phone compositions in the staging brief. An element fitting without overflow does not by itself establish the character's eyeline, reading order or payoff.
exceptions: Do not compress a 4.1-second intentional character scene into a sub-300 ms UI budget.
Keep keyboard Play available; immediate keyboard feedback rules do not remove access to requested performance content.
Do not remove expressive SVG anatomy to satisfy transform/opacity guidance without a measured relevant workload.
Do not treat character cause/effect ordering as forbidden menu stagger or impose a parent-entrance rule on the thought sequence.
Do not automatically delete the second peek: repetition may carry suspicion or hesitation and must be assessed in playback.
The vocabulary skill supplies precise names, not evidence of quality; catalog discovery alone does not invoke new libraries or prototype infrastructure.
